publication.title: Learning to Contextualize Web Pages for Enhanced Decision Making by LLM Agents

name: Learning to Contextualize Web Pages for Enhanced Decision Making by LLM Agents
notes: Reviewed against the ICLR 2025 proceedings page and PDF; the OpenReview forum lists it as an ICLR 2025 Poster. Experiments were not reproduced. LCoW's contextualization module reads the task, previous actions and a raw page observation such as an accessibility tree, and is retrained each iteration by supervised fine-tuning on the sampled rewrites that let several LLM agents recover the ground-truth action in successful trajectories. Appendix B fine-tunes Phi-3-mini-Instruct for WebShop and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct for WorkArena and WebArena. WebShop and WorkArena are the main benchmarks; a 165-task WebArena subset tests generalization to unseen task types. The same paper is posted on arXiv as 2503.10689 with the comment "Accepted to ICLR 2025". The paper points to lcowiclr2025.github.io for code, which was not reviewed here.
summary: Trains a separate language model to rewrite lengthy web page observations into focused descriptions for LLM web agents, keeping training targets that let several LLMs predict the correct next action.
